sakura-set.name: Sakura Set
sakura-set.description: Three hand-finished seasonal dice inspired by Japanese spring: soft sakura pink, wisteria purple, and matcha green. A free gift — enjoy!

metal-works.name: Metal Works
metal-works.description: Four metallic dice with real shine: polished silver, deep gunmetal, warm rose gold, and antique copper. Watch the light play as they tumble.

gemstones.name: Gemstones
gemstones.description: Four gem-cut dice with a jeweller's finish: imperial jade, midnight obsidian, royal sapphire, and blood-red ruby.

neon-glow.name: Neon Glow
neon-glow.tagline: Dice that light up the night
neon-glow.description: Four electric dice that glow from within: hot pink, cyber cyan, laser lime, and ultraviolet. Perfect on the marble table in a dark room.

tatami-room.name: Tatami Room
tatami-room.description: Bring the calm of a Japanese tatami room to your table, complete with a soft woven-straw surface that gently deadens each roll. Free for everyone.

casino-night.name: Casino Night
casino-night.description: Three professional casino surfaces: classic red baize, deep navy baize, and a polished walnut rail. Tuned physics give each table its own bounce.

party-night.name: Party Night Pack
party-night.description: Three fast, loud, luck-and-nerve dice games straight from the izakaya table: Chinchirorin, Cee-lo, and Drop Dead. Full illustrated rules included.

tavern-classics.name: Tavern Classics
tavern-classics.description: Three timeless tavern games — Shut the Box, Threes, and Going to Boston — with complete rules for game night.

chinchirorin.name: Chinchirorin
chinchirorin.summary: The classic Japanese bowl game. Three dice, up to three throws — pair two dice and score with the third!
rules: Each player antes into the pot, then players take turns as the roller.
Roll three dice into a bowl. If any die bounces out, the throw counts as a miss.
You get up to three throws to make a hand: a pair plus a single die — the single die is your score.
Special hands: 4-5-6 wins instantly, 1-2-3 loses instantly, and triples beat any normal score.
Three misses in a row is an automatic loss. The highest hand takes the pot.

cee-lo.name: Cee-lo
cee-lo.summary: A street-corner classic of instant wins, instant losses, and pure nerve.
rules: Players take turns rolling three dice until a scoring combination appears.
4-5-6 wins instantly; 1-2-3 loses instantly.
A pair plus a single die sets your point — the single die is your score.
Triples beat any point, and higher triples beat lower triples.
The banker plays each challenger head-to-head; the higher hand wins the stake.

drop-dead.name: Drop Dead
drop-dead.summary: A cheerful game of attrition — keep rolling until your dice drop dead.
rules: Roll all five dice. If no 2s or 5s appear, add the total to your score and roll all five again.
If any 2s or 5s appear, you score nothing for that throw and those dice are removed.
Keep rolling the remaining dice — every throw containing a 2 or 5 costs you those dice.
When your last die shows a 2 or 5, you're 'dead' and your turn ends.
Highest total score after everyone has played wins.

shut-the-box.name: Shut the Box
shut-the-box.summary: The centuries-old pub favourite of closing numbers and dodging penalties.
rules: Write the numbers 1 to 9 where everyone can see them; each player starts a turn with all nine numbers open.
Roll two dice and close any open numbers that add up exactly to the total (a roll of 9 can close 9, or 6+3, or 5+3+1).
Keep rolling and closing numbers. Once 7, 8 and 9 are all closed, you may choose to roll a single die instead.
When you can't close anything with a roll, your turn ends — the sum of your remaining open numbers is your penalty.
Close all nine numbers to 'shut the box' and win instantly; otherwise the lowest penalty after a full round wins.

threes.name: Threes
threes.summary: Low rolls win, and threes are gold — they count as zero.
rules: Roll five dice. Threes count as zero; every other die counts at face value.
After each roll you must set aside at least one die.
Re-roll the remaining dice until all five have been set aside.
Your score is the total of your kept dice — the lowest score wins the round.
Play five rounds; the lowest overall total takes the game.

going-to-boston.name: Going to Boston
going-to-boston.summary: A quick three-dice race that anyone can learn in a single round.
rules: Roll three dice and set aside the highest one.
Roll the remaining two dice and again set aside the highest.
Roll the last die — the sum of your three kept dice is your score.
Every player rolls in turn; the highest score wins the round.
First to win an agreed number of rounds — five works well — wins the game.
